description: Adaptive layout by width (schema 9.18.0): one table for every reader. Written by hand, not generated from the reference. Groups: classCases — the width class of a box; layerCases — which override layers act in a class; styleCases — «style» → «styleOn.medium» → «styleOn.expanded» → the first matching state of «styleWhen» («met» lists the data paths whose condition holds); propsCases — the effective props of a node in a class («propsOn», a closed list per widget); showCases — «showOn» together with «visibleIf»; drawnCases, numberCases, tabCases, weightCases, zoneCases, formCases — who counts as visible where the contract asks «visible»; validityCases — documents that are valid in one class and break a rule in another (nodes are given by type and by the fields that differ from a freshly created node; «on» is the class the issue belongs to, null — the base); contentCases — where the content of every screen zone stands with «Screen.contentMaxWidth», x from the LEFT edge of the root box; gridCases and boxCases — rectangles of children in the content box of the host on 393 / 768 / 1280 (the screen root has 16 of inline padding, so the content box is the frame minus 32), x from the left edge of the content box. Numbers are logical pixels and are never rounded. STEP 2 (wide places, the same schema 9.18.0) — «wideDefaults» holds the numbers the rows share (item and bar metrics of the default theme, heights for the zone rows, the margin of a window); chromeCases — who stands where in a class: the zones by the document and the place of the nav bar («bottom», «appBar» — its items inside the app bar, «top» — a bar of its own; «editor» is the place the editor draws when it differs, «navShown: false» — the bar is hidden in this class); wideNavItemCases, wideNavHeightCases — the width and the height of an item at the top; wideAppBarCases — the app bar with the nav items: rectangles from the LEFT edge of the screen box, «labels» are the natural widths of the labels of the drawn items, «bar» is what stands in the app bar (the box of the app bar has no padding of its own); wideNavBarCases — the same for the own top bar; wideZoneCases — the arithmetic of the screen zones in every combination of app bar × nav bar × pinned block × class («has» says what the screen has, the heights come from «wideDefaults.zone»); wideModalCases — a modal layer in an area: a sheet, a «center» window or a sheet shown as a window, and the width class of its content; wideModalRadiusCases — the root radius of a sheet shown as a window; wideSectionCases — two section screens whose nav bars name «widePlacement» (and, in the clarification, «showOn» of the bar and of its items: «bars[].showOn», «bars[].itemsShowOn» by the target of the item; a difference of the widths is reported with «what: widths»); wideModalContentCases — the width class of the content of a screen in an area of a class: a page takes the class of the area, a modal layer is always compact; olderReaderShowOnCases — a node with «showOn» that lacks «compact» is drawn on the phone by a reader older than 9.18 («affectsOlderReaderOnCompact»), and a node of the leading zone of the app bar then replaces the back arrow («replacesBackArrow»); wideRuleCases — the data of «x-style.layout» («wideNav», «wideModal»).

unsetNote: Schema 9.19.0 — an explicit «nothing» in a width layer: the key «unset» of «styleOn» and «propsOn» (rules: x-style.layout.widthUnset). «unsetStyleCases»: `node` carries «style» and «styleOn»; `expected` is the base style of the node on each class (null: no style) — what `styleOn` gives BEFORE the states. «unsetStateCases»: the style the node is drawn with on `widthClass` when the condition of its first state holds (`met`) or not. «unsetPropsCases»: `node` is a node of the type with «props» and «propsOn»; `expected` is the value of the property `prop` on each class (null: the property is absent). «unsetDocumentCases»: `node` stands on a screen as a child of the root; «unsetScreenCases»: `root` is the screen root itself; `schema` — the verdict of the JSON Schema (Zod and ajv agree), `codes` — the codes of the validator (empty: publishable). «readerOnly» — a document the builder does not make; the row says what a reader does with it.
